subject.title: [Feature]: Memory importance scoring + time decay for long-term memory

question: Should OpenClaw adopt durable memory importance scoring and decay as a memory-core/QMD contract, keep it plugin-owned, or defer it until the broader memory architecture changes?
rationale: The requested behavior affects persisted memory metadata, public config, backend parity, ranking semantics, and contradiction handling, so automation cannot safely choose the product/API contract.

options.title: Design memory contract first
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers define the canonical importance metadata, decay/access policy, QMD parity contract, contradiction handling, and upgrade plan before implementation.

options.title: Accept a narrow opt-in subset
options.body: Allow a smaller opt-in temporal-decay or importance-weighting feature only if it uses one documented config path and includes upgrade/proof coverage.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned for now
options.body: Require external memory plugins or ClawHub packages to own scoring policy until OpenClaw decides a stable shared memory API is needed.

recommendation.title: Design memory contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this open while maintainers define the canonical importance metadata, decay/access policy, QMD parity contract, contradiction handling, and upgrade plan before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the major memory-core plugin refactor that owns the relevant current files and is the best available routing candidate from git history.
